applies_to: Trane Series R RTWD water-cooled and RTUD condenserless helical-rotary chillers with CH530 controls fitted with the BCI2-C BACnet interface.
summary: The BCI2-C is a non-programmable Trane controller that connects to the CH530 chiller controls over the IPC3 link and serves the chiller data on BACnet MS/TP. This list is the RTWD column of the guide's model tables: 102 objects with low instance numbers. The BAS writes chilled and hot water setpoints and current limit (AO), auto/stop and diagnostic reset (BO) and chiller mode (MO); everything else is read-only water, refrigerant, oil, compressor and electrical data.
notes: The guide's tables mark each object against RTWD, RTUD, RTHD, RTAC, CGAM/CXAM and CGWN/CCUN; this file holds the RTWD column. The RTUD column is the same except that it adds AI 42/43 Airflow Percentage (circuits 1 and 2), and the AO setpoint table has no RTUD column.
The BCI2-C self-configures, so only the objects that match the connected chiller show up.
The tables have no read/write column: AI/BI/MI are read-only, and the AO/BO/MO objects (listed with relinquish defaults) are the BAS setpoints and commands, marked writable here.

Units are given as a quantity (Temperature, Pressure, Percent...); SI or I-P follows the BCI2-C Device Units setting. Two printing slips are corrected here: AI 12 is described as circuit 2 in the guide, and BI 24's active state is printed 'None' (it means alarm).
On RTWD, AO 4 Hot Water Setpoint is for leaving condenser water temperature control, and AI 24 Unit Power Consumption needs the power meter option.
Trane's Symbio 800 'RTWD (CH530)' points list (BAS-PTS035A) uses the same numbering but lists only 47 analog inputs; this guide adds the AO/BO/MO commands and the BI/MI status objects.

source.title: Integration Guide: BACnet Communication Interface for Chillers (BCI2-C)

integration.summary: Address the BCI2-C on the MS/TP trunk and discover it. Write BO 1 auto/stop, MO 1 mode, AO 1 chilled water setpoint and AO 2 current limit, then read back running state, leaving water temperature and capacity. BI 23 Alarm Present and BI 24 Shutdown Alarm Present are the summary alarms, and BI 25 shows the last diagnostic.

integration.enable: BO 1 Chiller Auto Stop Command (Inactive = Stop, Active = Auto; relinquish default True, i.e. Auto) is the BMS auto/stop. BI 1 Run Enabled shows whether the chiller is available to run, and BI 2 Local Setpoint Control shows when the chiller is using local setpoints instead of the BAS setpoints.
setup: The BCI2-C is a BACnet MS/TP device only (EIA-485 at 9600, 19200, 38400 or 76,800 bps); the default baud rate is 76,800.

It has no physical rotary dials: the factory address is on a label on the board and is changed in the embedded BCI2 Service Tool (USB, browser at 198.80.18.1) or Tracer TU. Valid MAC addresses are 001-127.
The default software Device ID equals the MAC address; tick 'Use Software Device ID' to set another one. A Tracer SC builds its own device ID from the SC address, link number and MAC.
Communicated units default to SI once the points are created. To switch to I-P, clear the controller with the IPC3 cable unplugged (or the unit powered down) so the Device Units choice unlocks.
For non-Trane front ends, set Max Master (Max Requestor) above the BCI2-C MAC address or the device will not be discovered.
gotchas: The BCI2-C builds its point list from the CH530 controller at first power-up and stores it. If options are added later, clear the controller so it rebuilds the list.
BO 2 Remote Diagnostic Reset Command: after a write of 1 the BCI2-C sends the reset, sets the point back to 0 and clears the priority array. Some diagnostics still need a local reset.

With the external (hard-wired) setpoint option, the chiller follows the external setpoints when the CH530 setpoint source is External/Front Panel, when the setpoint AO is set Out of Service, or when a Tracer SC loses communication with the BCI2-C.
MI 3 MP Communication Status is marked 'Do Not Use This Point' in the document.
